label: First copy-phase step echoing a leading digit 1 (long sequences)
explanation: Fires only at the first copy step after <DEL> (recall_idx == 1, prev_tok = <DEL>), when the input fed back is the digit 1, which means the sequence began with 1 (first_tok == 1). It fires only for long sequences (L >= 6) and never for L <= 5. Magnitude grows with L: L=6 activations are weak and fire inconsistently (most of the false positives are L=6 cases with no activation), and L=9 carries the largest share of the activation mass. Which token is output next makes little difference. It does not fire in the original or delimiter phases, on later copy steps, or when the first token is anything other than 1 (there are a handful of near-zero activations when the first token is 2 or q).

issues: Every factual claim checks out on dev and test. All activation mass is in the copy phase at recall_idx == 1 with in_tok = 1. Nothing fires for L = 3..5. Within L >= 7 the predicate has precision 1.0. Across L = 7, 8 and 9 the number of active steps is about the same (2809, 2690, 2767) while the mass share rises (0.207, 0.328, 0.438), so magnitude does grow with L.

Almost all of the 1062 test false positives are L = 6 cases (the single dev false positive at L >= 7 is '1 g 1 1 k s t'). At L = 6 the feature fires on only about 61% of predicted steps and its activations are weak (about 0.01 to 0.16 of max), holding 2.7% of the mass. This matches the explanation's 'weak and inconsistent' description.

Minor overclaim: 'which token is output next makes little difference' is not quite true at L = 6. Precision is about 0.83 when the output token is a digit and about 0.58 when it is a letter. Whether 1 repeats among the original tokens also matters at L = 6 (in_count >= 2 gives precision 0.39 versus 0.66 when 1 appears once). For L >= 7 neither condition matters (precision is about 1.0). I found no clean rule that separates the L = 6 firings from the non-firings, so I count this residual as graded, low-magnitude behaviour rather than a systematic missed class.
Missed activations: 3 on test, all with first token 2 followed by 1 and activation 0.04 or less. This is negligible noise.

Alternative predicate (recall_idx == 1) & (in_tok == tok('1')) & (L >= 7) gives test precision 1.0, recall 0.83, F1 0.908 and mass recall 0.973. That is worse than the original's F1 of 0.95, so the original predicate stands.
